shouldFix.title: The entry records a candidate without stating that it binds nothing, which every other recording in this branch states
shouldFix.finding: Decision item 1 reads 'Record provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6.json as DR-133's leftover-design measurement candidate. Both independent reviewers returned 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.' It does not say the candidate binds nothing. I checked the branch: D-136 says 'Candidate binds NOTHING', D-138 says 'The candidate binds NOTHING', and so do D-137, D-131 and D-116 — five of five recordings, including both entries this one names as its branch. The entry's own predecessor draft said it too, at its Decision item 1. The artifact itself carries binds NOTHING and status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, so the recording is dropping a bound the artifact asserts about itself. It matters more here than in a typical recording, because what v6 contains is a set of forward-looking assignments — five NT classes said to be capable of riding two named live gates, each carried with that gate's own owner cell. A reader who takes the recorded candidate as operative would read those as live gate assignments, which is precisely what the artifact spent six versions learning not to claim. Decision item 2's bounds are about the row's readiness — OPEN, not SATISFIED, gates 2 and 3 not holding — and do not say anything about the artifact's force.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: Nothing recorded is false, and item 3 makes clear that the riding classes are not yet named at their gates. The defect is a missing bound that the branch applies without exception.
shouldFix.repair: Add the clause to Decision item 1, in the branch's own words: 'The candidate binds NOTHING.'
evidence: COORD 64d76c32…, D-136, D-138, D-137, D-131 and D-116 Decision paragraphs — all five state the candidate binds NOTHING

At the moment this draft was written the statement was defensible, since the join dispatch and this draft share a timestamp and no verdict existed yet. shouldFix.repair: Say what happened. Two sentences will do: name coordinator-decisions.D-143.join.draft.md at its digest as the withdrawn predecessor of this entry, state that it is not adopted and that its cycle is closed by this renumbering, and keep the separate sentence about the unreviewed G23 draft. That leaves no D-143 artifact unaccounted for.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 2 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, three landed. Custody is clean: fa444127 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 2d1254e, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all seven measured inputs reproduce. This is a better draft than the join draft it replaces, and its best part is Decision item 3, which creates the owed D-086 obligation explicitly and in the branch's own form — a successor in its own D-000 cycle that must name the riding NT classes at the G20 and G21 obligations the way DR-102's CC-1..CC-11 are named at G21, with the NT-3 and NT-5 path kept separate. That was exactly the gap I charged in the predecessor draft. Its summary of the artifact matches v6 field for field, five capable-of-riding and two leftover, with capable-of-riding not upgraded to riding and gates 2 and 3 stated not to hold. It represents my own v6 verdict exactly, at ACCEPT 0/0 with CLAUDE-PONGJ-V6-ADV1; the Codex half of the dual-ACCEPT claim I could only confirm as a digest, having hashed that file without opening it. Two things block. First, Decision item 1 records the candidate without saying it binds nothing. Every recording in this branch says it — D-136, D-138, D-137, D-131 and D-116, five of five, including both entries this one cites as its branch — and the join draft said it too, and the artifact itself carries binds NOTHING. It matters here because what v6 contains is five forward-looking assignments to two named live gates carried with those gates' owners, which is exactly the content a reader might take as operative; item 2's bounds speak to the row's readiness, not to the artifact's force. Second, the entry says D-143 is an unreviewed G23 draft, but D-143 also names coordinator-decisions.D-143.join.draft.md, frozen at 0444 with its own dispatch and prompt, which a diff shows is this entry's direct predecessor and which now carries a Claude 2 verdict. That was defensible when this draft was written, since the two share a timestamp, but adoption comes later and would record a statement that is false of that subject while leaving an OBJECTed predecessor with no disposition. Two sentences naming it as withdrawn would close it. The advisory is that the COORD-scope refusal, present in the join draft and in D-142, was dropped again — the third time across five entries, which suggests it belongs in the template rather than in each author's discretion.
